clue.text: Rock star in movies

parts.note: a rock is a stone, which is this film star's surname
a Hollywood actress, best known for Basic Instinct

explanation.surface: A rock musician turns up on the cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Every across clue in this puzzle clues one half of a famous name; the grid takes the other half. Here rock gives STONE, so Sharon Stone's first name is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharon Stone is an American film actress, so her first name identifies a movie star.

clue.text: Pass around Guardian readers' drape

indicators.note: the word for passing time is wrapped around the readers' pronoun

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
the setter speaks to the paper's own readers, so they are 'us'

explanation.surface: A newspaper reader hands round a curtain belonging to fellow subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape cloth is to hang it loosely, which is what suspending it means.

clue.text: Leading actor's first on the block

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so the letter comes above the head
the opening letter of the word actor is wanted

parts.note: the word actor, from which only the opening letter is taken
block is slang for the head, as in 'knock your block off'

explanation.surface: The star of the show is the first to face the executioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the block' suggests execution, but block is simply slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ahead is in front, in the lead, so ahead works as a synonym for leading.

clue.text: Disillusioned with certain politicians' "no bull here"

parts.note: to go off something is to lose your liking for it
the centre is the political middle ground and those who hold it

explanation.surface: A voter sick of moderates declares they will hear no nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is the bullseye at the centre of a target, so a shot that lands elsewhere is off-centre; 'bull' as nonsense is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot that misses the target's middle has not scored a bullseye, a cryptic description of being off-centre.

clue.text: Novelist's quarter

parts.note: the clued writer is a British novelist and critic
west is one quarter of the compass, and also the writer's surname

explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the surname WEST, a compass quarter; the grid takes the novelist's first name, Rebecca.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca West was the pen name of the British author of The Return of the Soldier and other novels.

clue.text: Rex goes off with fencing strips

parts.note: Latin for king, abbreviated R as in royal signatures
an egg that addles has gone bad

explanation.surface: A dog named Rex runs off taking some swordplay gear with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fencing' suggests swordplay, but these are the thin wooden strips woven into a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Raddles are flexible rods or laths interwoven to make a wattle fence or hedge.

clue.text: Weedy thing the troops might get aroused by

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low-growing creeping plant often treated as a weed

definitions.text: the troops might get aroused by
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the brass instrument that sounds reveille in camp

explanation.surface: A puny item that could still rouse a camp of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a creeping blue-flowered plant (ajuga) and the military horn that wakes soldiers.

clue.text: Nutcase he employed as a singer

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a fresh arrangement, so they are worked over

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material, used as written

explanation.surface: A lunatic was taken on as the band's vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanteuse is a female nightclub or cabaret vocalist, the French word for a woman who sings.

clue.text: The poet's tired of each entry in "Twisted"

indicators.note: the abbreviation for each is entered into the word for twisted

parts.note: something askew or crooked has gone awry

explanation.surface: A poet grows weary of every item in a collection called Twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The poet's' marks the word as literary or archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Aweary is an old poetic form meaning weary, worn out.

clue.text: Scoffs immoderately at empty politician's pen

parts.note: to pig out is to eat greedily, so one who pigs scoffs immoderately

indicators.note: the middle of the politician's label is taken away, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a hollow MP's writing implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' reads as a writing tool, but it is the enclosure for swine.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is an enclosure for animals, and a pigsty is the pen where swine are kept.

clue.text: Linesman in no time at all collars fool

definitions.text: Linesman in no time at all collars fool

parts.note: a writer of lines of verse, a poet, rather than a football official

parts.words: in no time at all collars fool
parts.note: soon around ass spells the poet's surname, SASSOON

explanation.surface: A referee's assistant catches out an idiot in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: Soon (in no time at all) around ass (fool) gives SASSOON; the grid takes the war poet's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon was a First World War poet, and a poet is a man of lines.

clue.text: Honey: the British life-saver

parts.note: an endearment, like darling, which is the heroine's surname
a lighthouse keeper's daughter who rowed out to rescue shipwrecked sailors in 1838

explanation.surface: A sweet tribute to a national rescuer.
explanation.walkthrough: Honey gives DARLING; the grid takes the first name of Grace Darling, the Northumberland rescue heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace Darling became a Victorian national heroine for saving survivors of the wrecked steamer Forfarshire.

clue.text: Comic Brummie with comic sleep indicator and a flipping doctor

definitions.text: Comic Brummie with comic sleep indicator and a flipping doctor

parts.note: a stand-up comedian, the person whose names the clue is after

parts.words: with comic sleep indicator and a flipping doctor
parts.note: ZZ (the snoring of a cartoon sleeper), A, and DR turned round build the end of the surname IZZARD

explanation.surface: A Birmingham comedian dozes off beside a doctor doing somersaults.
explanation.walkthrough: ZZ + A + reversed DR gives -ZZARD of IZZARD; the grid takes Eddie Izzard's first name. How 'Brummie' supplies the opening I is not clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Izzard is a British stand-up comedian famous for surreal, rambling routines.

clue.text: The real Doctor Who player?

parts.note: the real McCoy means the genuine article, and McCoy is the actor's surname
the actor who played the seventh Doctor in the BBC science-fiction series

explanation.surface: Which actor is the genuine Time Lord?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The real' gives McCOY, from 'the real McCoy'; the grid takes the first name of Sylvester McCoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvester McCoy starred as the Doctor in Doctor Who from 1987 to 1989.

clue.text: Funny writer's "Winter Jacket" on the radio

definitions.text: Funny writer's "Winter Jacket" on the radio

parts.note: the American wit famous for her one-liners and verse
a parka spoken aloud is the writer's surname, PARKER

explanation.surface: A humorist's piece called Winter Jacket is broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The parka homophone gives PARKER; the grid takes Dorothy Parker's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy Parker was an American humorist celebrated for her wisecracks and satirical writing.

clue.text: Study sound: it could be a mouth instrument

indicators.note: the word for study is said out loud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it
the mouth is one example of a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A student studies acoustics and wonders whether a harmonica counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth instrument' suggests a mouth organ, but the mouth is just an example of an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ is a keyboard instrument such as the harmonium, sounding by vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Nietzschean eye-opening poet in hiding

parts.note: the letters that conceal the surname, running across these words
a poet's name concealed in the preceding words: HEANEY

explanation.surface: A philosopher's revelation about a reclusive versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: HEANEY lies in nietzscHEAN EYE-opening; the grid takes Seamus Heaney's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamus Heaney was the Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1995.

clue.text: It's stimulating, dinner a la mode

indicators.note: after 'a la' the word suggests a new fashion, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: these letters, taken as written, are the raw material

explanation.surface: A menu promises an exciting meal served in the fashionable style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A la mode' looks like one cookery phrase, but 'a la' belongs to the letters and only 'mode' signals the change.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone that stimulates the body's fight-or-flight response.

clue.text: Bunter is in business as a cosmetician

definitions.text: Bunter is in business as a cosmetician

parts.note: these letters rearrange to the surname RUBINSTEIN
the founder of a global beauty-products empire

explanation.surface: Billy Bunter, the fat schoolboy of comic stories, sets up as a beautician.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffling BUNTER IS IN gives RUBINSTEIN; the grid takes Helena Rubinstein's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena Rubinstein built one of the first international cosmetics companies.

clue.text: Rolling TV news aid?

parts.note: suggests rolling news, the round-the-clock channel, but it is the scrolling text
the device a newsreader reads the script from

explanation.surface: A tool for twenty-four-hour news channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling news' is continuous broadcasting; here it is the script itself that rolls up the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade-named prompter scrolls the script in front of the camera lens for presenters to read.

clue.text: Cleaner who became a US president

definitions.text: Cleaner who became a US president

parts.note: a Hoover is a vacuum cleaner, and Hoover is the president's surname
the thirty-first American head of state

explanation.surface: A janitor's unlikely rise to the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaner gives HOOVER, the British word for a vacuum cleaner; the grid takes Herbert Hoover's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Hoover served as the thirty-first president of the United States, from 1929 to 1933.

clue.text: The man to pardon wife, about the fourth of Vicar of Bray

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the pardon and the wife enclose the chosen letter

parts.note: 'Eh?' asks someone to repeat themselves, as 'Pardon?' does

indicators.note: the letter in fourth place of the word Vicar

parts.note: the word Vicar, counted along to its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A man forgives his wife over something to do with the Vicar of Bray, the famous turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray, from the old song, kept changing his faith to hold his parish; here Bray is just a donkey's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw imitates a donkey's call, which is what a bray is.

clue.text: T-take sick and die back

parts.note: the stammered T plus ail, to fall ill
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A stuttering patient says they will get ill and fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter supplies a lone T before the word for being unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the rear part of something, the back of it.

clue.text: You could say sheep look for land abroad

indicators.note: the words are spoken aloud to give a near sound-alike

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: A sheep peers about in search of foreign pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: A gander is British slang for a look, as in 'have a gander'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an East African country, a foreign land to a British solver.

clue.text: "Popular writer", I say, and point to King

definitions.text: "Popular writer", I say, and point to King

parts.note: a best-selling author of Regency romances

parts.words: I say, and point to King
parts.note: hey (I say) plus E (a compass point) and R (king) spells the surname HEYER

explanation.surface: Someone praises a best-selling author and gestures towards a monarch, or towards Stephen King.
explanation.walkthrough: Hey + E + R gives HEYER; the grid takes Georgette Heyer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgette Heyer wrote hugely popular Regency romance and detective novels.

clue.text: Pinched top? Crooks leg it!

indicators.note: to crook is to bend out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: the phrase for running away, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Thieves make off with stolen clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooks' reads as thieves fleeing; it is a verb meaning bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless jacket, a garment one might call a top, and the question mark admits it is a stolen one.

clue.text: Model playing the queen at "Telephone Company"

definitions.text: Model playing the queen at "Telephone Company"

parts.note: a supermodel of the 1990s
camp (acting the queen) and Bell (the telephone company) make the surname CAMPBELL

explanation.surface: A fashion model takes the role of a monarch in a play called Telephone Company.
explanation.walkthrough: Camp + Bell gives CAMPBELL; the grid takes Naomi Campbell's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi Campbell is a British supermodel, one of the best-known catwalk models of her era.

clue.text: Hardly the Gold Route excursion

indicators.note: the letters go off on a trip and come back rearranged

parts.note: the word is used as written, its letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sightseeing trip that is no golden road.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the gold is the bullseye at the target's centre; the outer is the outermost ring, as far from it as can score.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer ring of an archery target is the opposite of the central gold.

clue.text: Piece to market racing driver

parts.note: man (a piece in chess or draughts) plus sell (to market) spells the surname MANSELL
the British Formula One world champion of 1992

explanation.surface: A dealer wants to sell a chess piece to someone who races cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Man + sell gives MANSELL; the grid takes Nigel Mansell's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Mansell won the Formula One world championship in 1992, a celebrated British motor-racing champion.

clue.text: Singer's place most likely to see public debut of gospel singer

definitions.text: Singer's place most likely to see public debut of gospel singer

parts.note: a choir sings in church, which is this singer's surname

parts.words: most likely to see public debut of gospel singer
parts.note: a hymn singer would first perform in church

explanation.surface: Where would a gospel vocalist first sing in public?
explanation.walkthrough: The place is CHURCH; the grid takes the first name of Charlotte Church, the Welsh soprano who became famous as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer who found fame with sacred and classical songs.

clue.text: Name cherished by living US film actress

definitions.text: Name cherished by living US film actress

parts.note: N (name) held inside being (living) spells the surname BENING
the American star of American Beauty

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actress whose name is treasured while she is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: N inside BEING gives BENING; the grid takes Annette Bening's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Annette Bening is an American actress, Oscar-nominated for American Beauty and other films.

clue.text: Oscar-winning star, "Mr Bean", is lost without a lot of money

definitions.text: Oscar-winning star, "Mr Bean", is lost without a lot of money

parts.note: a Swedish actress who won three Academy Awards

parts.words: "Mr Bean", is lost without a lot of money
parts.note: MR BEAN rearranged around G (a grand, a lot of money) spells the surname BERGMAN

explanation.surface: A comic character is broke without a fortune, despite an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's bumbling TV character. Shuffled round G, his name gives BERGMAN; the grid takes Ingrid Bergman's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid Bergman, star of Casablanca, won three Academy Awards for acting.
